{{Quote|Since earliest memory the enemies of the Prajii had been the Vahalii and the Juonii.|Doctor Gabrel Treon, "Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji: A Cartel of Genes"|<ref name="TTSP" />}}
'''House Vahali''', members of which were known as the '''Vahalii''', was a [[Great House]] that was based on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kaikielius/Legends|Kaikielius]] during the rule of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Along with its rivals, [[House Juoni]] and [[House Praji/Legends|House Praji]], House Vahali formed part of the [[Triad (Great Houses)|Triad]], and the three families collectively held much influence on the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the Republic's [[Capital/Legends|capital]]. Eventually, House Juoni collapsed and House Praji departed Kaikielius, leaving the world to the Vahalii. Members of House Vahali were elected to all levels of the Kaikieli government, but the family faced problems as a result of the rising power of criminal factions on Kaikielius. However, the criminals were eventually [[Kaikieli Reconquista|driven]] from Kaikielius in [[4225 BBY]], leaving House Vahali free to reconstruct the world. Thousands of [[Standard year/Legends|years]] later, [[Nahdonnis Praji]] of House Praji conquered Kaikielius during [[Operation Shadow Hand]], shattering House Vahali's power base. The Vahalii later reemerged on the planet [[Denon/Legends|Denon]], where they attempted to build a new sphere of influence for themselves.

==History==
{{Quote|The Reconquista was devastating but effective, and once the Hutts and other undesirables had been driven out, the Vahalii were free to rebuild as they wished.|Doctor Gabrel Treon, "Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji: A Cartel of Genes"|<ref name="TTSP" />}}
House Vahali was an aristocratic family that lived on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kaikielius/Legends|Kaikielius]] during the rule of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. From early in their history, the Vahalii considered themselves the enemies of [[House Praji/Legends|House Praji]], another Kaikieli family. According to legend, the Vahalii were descended from the original colonists of Kaikielius, who had fragmented as a result of a doctrinal dispute and divided themselves into three groups&mdash;House Vahali, House Praji, and [[House Juoni]]. However, the [[Historian/Legends|historian]] [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Gabrel Treon]] later speculated that the legend was untrue and that the three Houses were just the strongest of a number of families vying for control on Kaikielius. Regardless of their origins, the Vahalii, the Juonii, and the Prajii eventually institutionalized themselves and became [[Great House]]s that were collectively known as the [[Triad (Great Houses)|Triad]]. Jointly, the three houses held much influence on the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of the Republic. The families began competing against each other, and, on occasion, the Vahalii absorbed lesser Kaikieli families into themselves or bribed them into working against the interests of the Juonii and the Prajii.<ref name="TTSP" />

House Juonii eventually collapsed as a result of its role in the [[First Alsakan Conflict]], leaving Kaikielius to House Vahali and House Praji. The two houses continued to plot against each other, and their dissension prevented Kaikielius from gaining primacy over its rival world, [[Empress Teta/Legends|Koros]]. Following the [[Unification Wars (Koros)/Legends|unification]] of the [[Empress Teta system/Legends|Koros system]] in [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], Kaikielius experienced large-scale industrial growth in an attempt to compete with Koros, leading to widespread urban development on Kaikielius. As a result, the world attracted the attention of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], and both the Vahalii and the Prajii began losing [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] as a result of Hutt operations on Kaikielius.<ref name="TTSP" />

The Praji family relocated to Coruscant in [[4800 BBY]], and, in their absence, members of House Vahali were elected to positions at all levels of Kaikielius' government. However, criminal factions began to become increasingly powerful on the world, and the Vahalii struggled to maintain control. For sixty [[Standard year/Legends|years]], [[Emppu Praji-Barck]], the Republic [[Minister of State]] and a member of the Praji family, prevented the Republic from coming to the aide of House Vahali, and conditions on Kaikielius worsened. Eventually, the Prajii bribed the Hutt [[Odominic]] kajidic into supplying arms to criminals on Kaikielius, causing a war to develop on the planet between the criminal gangs and the world's [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|police]] force. The escalated conflict forced the Republic to intervene, and it sent [[Troop/Legends|troops]] to Kaikielius in [[4225 BBY]], during what became known as the [[Kaikieli Reconquista]]. The [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Derrica Praji]], another member of the Praji family, fought alongside the Republic forces on Kaikielius and helped them to retake the planet from the criminals, despite knowing that by doing so, he was aiding the Vahalii and thereby negating centuries of scheming carried out by his family. In the aftermath of the Reconquista, House Vahali was left free to reconstruct Kaikielius, and the Prajii were angered that their schemes against the Vahalii had failed.<ref name="TTSP" />

By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], over four thousand years later, House Vahali had established its headquarters in a [[Skyhook/Legends|skyhook]] that [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] Kaikielius. During [[Operation Shadow Hand]] in [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]], [[Nahdonnis Praji]] of the Praji family led [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] forces in an [[Battle of Kaikielius (Galactic Civil War)|attack]] on Kaikielius, and he knocked the Vahalii skyhook out of orbit. The destruction of its headquarters and the subsequent Imperial occupation of Kaikielius shattered the power base of House Vahali, forcing it into poverty. The Vahalii eventually resurfaced on the planet [[Denon/Legends|Denon]], where they attempted to build a new sphere of influence for themselves. Gabrel Treon later wrote about the Vahalii in "[[Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji: A Cartel of Genes]]," a history of the Praji family that was published in the ''[[Byblos Journal of Historical Science]]''<ref name="TTSP" /> in [[104 ABY]].<ref name="TTSP end notes">{{Blog|valinkenobi|14/comments|TTSP Endnotes: Volume 1}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
House Vahali was created by [[Nathan O'Keefe]] and featured in ''[[Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji]]'', an article that was published in the [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] section of the website [[StarWars.com]] in [[2009]].<ref name="TTSP" />
